meta.title: Forma
meta.subtitle: Turn complex work into clear form

narrative.question: What is Forma, and when should a team use it?
narrative.summary: Forma is a spec-first compiler for visual technical communication. An Agent turns source material into structured content; a deterministic renderer turns that spec into a polished, self-contained HTML document; browser QA checks that the result is accessible, responsive, and offline.
takeaways: The Agent owns meaning, narrative, source attribution, and block selection
The renderer owns layout, typography, accessibility, and consistency
The result is one portable HTML file with zero external requests

sections.title: Forma
sections.subtitle: Turn complex work into clear form

sections.statement: Forma separates understanding the work from presenting it well.
sections.qualifier: An Agent decides what the material means. A deterministic compiler decides how that meaning becomes a readable, reliable browser document.

sections.title: A reliable path from raw material to a document people can use
sections.body:
Give Forma documents, code, diffs, test results, or working notes. The Agent reads the material and writes `forma.spec.json`: a structured account of the narrative, semantic blocks, sources, and confidence behind each claim. The renderer then compiles that spec into one browser-ready page and checks the result.

The boundary is deliberate. Agents are good at interpreting context; a maintained renderer is better at producing consistent layout, typography, accessibility, and security every time.

sections.claim: The Agent writes structured intent, not one-off HTML and CSS.
sections.detail: The spec records the document's purpose, audience, sources, narrative, and semantic blocks. Forma validates that structure before rendering it. This turns important communication rules—such as citing a verified claim or including a data timestamp—into build-time contracts instead of prompt suggestions.

sections.title: One source-to-document pipeline owns each responsibility

sections.claim: Four artifact contracts make the reader's job part of the document structure.
sections.detail: A dashboard must expose current state and freshness. A report must put its conclusion and recommendation up front. A manual must pair steps with verification and recovery. An advanced artifact must connect a decision to evidence and preserve the outcome. These are validation contracts, not visual themes.

sections.title: Choose the artifact by the answer the reader needs

cells.Required shape: Status, KPI, change, driver, action, freshness
Brief, evidence graph, alternatives, decision record

sections.claim: The deliverable is portable by construction and private by default.
sections.detail: Fonts, styles, diagrams, and the small interaction layer are embedded into the output. Opening the rendered file makes zero external network requests. Inputs are escaped and sanitized, while secret and local-path redaction add a final safety layer before the file is written.

sections.title: The product claims are backed by code-level boundaries

items.summary: The renderer does not call a model
items.detail: Model-assisted interpretation ends at the structured spec. Rendering is a local TypeScript pipeline.

items.summary: Every rendered string crosses a sanitization boundary
items.detail: Plain text, inline Markdown, SVG, and URLs each have a documented escape or allowlist path.
Forma checks external requests, accessibility, console errors, overflow, responsive viewports, reduced motion, dark mode, and JavaScript-disabled behavior.

sections.statement: Use Forma when complex technical material needs to become a document another person can understand, verify, or act on.
sections.rationale: It is strongest where narrative quality, source traceability, repeatable presentation, and offline sharing matter together: engineering reviews, test reports, release gates, operating procedures, and decision records.
conditions: Do not use Forma to build a marketing landing page or a general application UI
Do not treat renderer validation as proof that a source claim is true
Use Advanced Room Mode only when local live collaboration is explicitly required
sections.notes: This recommendation combines the product brief's intended uses and non-goals.

sections.title: The boundaries are as important as the features

risks.description: Using Forma where bespoke visual expression is the primary goal
risks.mitigation: Use a purpose-built design or application workflow for marketing pages and product UI

risks.description: Mistaking a valid spec for verified source truth
risks.mitigation: Keep source references precise and mark unsupported claims inferred or unknown

risks.description: Describing Advanced Room Mode as fully offline
risks.mitigation: State that external requests remain zero while explicitly requested local network traffic may occur

sections.title: Try Forma on work you already need to explain

items.label: Install dependencies and build Forma with `pnpm install && pnpm build`
Invoke `$forma` or `/forma` with source material and the reader's goal
Open the rendered HTML and review its sources, confidence labels, and QA result
